title: It’s a Draw… Right? A Bishop Check Before the Fork
summary: Answer the rook check with a bishop sacrifice, then use king restriction and knight forks to reach exact winning endings.

nodes.question: Can White answer the rook check while keeping both winning ideas?
nodes.explanation: Bb5+ blocks the b-file check and checks Ka4. Either capture lets White remove the rook or force it into a capture or fork after Ka2.

branches.title: Source defense: the king takes the bishop
commentary: Begin after ...Rb8+ with White Kb2/Be2/Nd7/a3/g4 against Ka4/Rb8/a5/g5. Both pairs of pawns remain in the complete later board.
Bb5+ interposes on the b-file and counterchecks the black king along b5–a4. Black has exactly two legal captures.
Kxb5 accepts the bishop with the king. The rook remains on b8, where Nd7 can capture it.
Nxb8 captures the rook and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. Removing the bishop means this ending is not the earlier two-bishop stalemate trap.
branches.explanation: Nxb8 captures the rook and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. Removing the bishop means this ending is not the earlier two-bishop stalemate trap.

branches.title: Source defense: rook capture and pawn recapture
commentary: Compare the rook capture instead of the king capture, preserving the full a- and g-pawn structure.
Bb5+ blocks the rook check and checks Ka4 with the offered bishop.
Rxb5+ removes the bishop and renews the b-file check against Kb2.
Ka2 is the source king move. It controls b3 while the a3 pawn controls b4; the knight and blocked pawns leave Black only rook moves.
Rf5 is the source rook sacrifice, moving from b5 along the fifth rank. The white g4 pawn can capture it.
gxf5 removes the rook and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. Black’s g5 pawn remains on the board; the branch does not erase it or assume a later promotion race.
branches.explanation: gxf5 removes the rook and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. Black’s g5 pawn remains on the board; the branch does not erase it or assume a later promotion race.

branches.title: Independent defense: move the rook to d5
commentary: Test a legal rook move along the fifth rank. This completion is an independent representative defense.
Bb5+ offers the bishop with an interposing check.
Rxb5+ takes the bishop and checks Kb2.
Ka2 restricts the black king and leaves the rook to move.
Rd5 avoids the immediate pawn capture on f5, but steps onto a knight-fork square.
Nb6+ checks Ka4 and attacks Rd5 at the same time.
Kb5 is forced. The a5 pawn occupies a5, White’s a3 pawn controls b4, and Ka2 controls b3.
Nxd5 captures the rook. The exact seven-piece ending is a White win with all four pawns retained.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Nxd5 captures the rook. The exact seven-piece ending is a White win with all four pawns retained.

branches.title: Independent defense: move the rook to b7
commentary: Test a rook retreat along the b-file instead of the source’s rook sacrifice.
Bb5+ first answers the rook check and forces a capture.
Rxb5+ accepts the bishop and checks Kb2.
Ka2 creates the same restricted king position.
Rb7 retreats but lies on a square attacked by a knight arriving on c5.
Nc5+ checks Ka4 and attacks Rb7.
Kb5 is the only legal king reply, leaving the rook available to capture.
Nxb7 removes the rook and reaches an exact seven-piece White win. These added king/rook choices are not attributed to an unseen original game score.

exercises.answer: White is in check from Rb8. Bb5 interposes with a countercheck and forces one of two captures.
Ka2 controls b3 and a3 controls b4. Black’s king and pawns cannot move, while each rook move allows a capture or checking knight fork.

startContext: Begin after ...Rb8+ at 128 seconds in the complete nine-piece later source variation. All a- and g-pawns are retained. The source Rf5/gxf5 finish is included; two representative rook-fork completions are explicitly independent. The earlier rook sacrifice, bishop interference and claimed drawn alternatives remain outside this selected proof.
